tools.title: Context recall — session episodic + identity memory
tools.description: Read-only recall of the current session's episodic memory plus durable identity/user context — never writes. Scope: the optional `brain_id` (otherwise BRAIN_ID or the nearest `.brain/config.json` from the caller-provided project working directory (or the MCP process working directory when absent)), limited to the request metadata session id (falling back to BRAIN_KHORTEX_SESSION, read at call time and REQUIRED; when both are unset this tool refuses with a scoped-session-required error and runs no query, since an unscoped cross-session recall is an unauthenticated data exposure). Precedence: when the call carries a session id, that session's PINNED brain outranks `brain_id` — the answer then comes from the pinned brain, the output names both brains in a `brain override:` line, and the serve logs the ignored drift. No approval needed — it only reads. Trust: completeness promise — if it happened it is found; if it did not, this tool says so plainly rather than guessing, and grounded answers carry provenance. Reversible by nature: a read changes nothing.

tools.name: brain_requests_list
tools.title: Requests — the brain's recent requests with their verdicts
tools.description: Read-only list of the brain's recent requests (search, ask, recall, sync …), newest first, from the committed query traces. Each row names the notes the request returned (top 10 hits), its outcome, confidence and latency. Query text appears only when the brain opted in (brains.query_text_opt_in, default off); otherwise the row carries its sha256 alone. Verdicts come from brain_feedback_events: a human verdict outranks a machine one, and `verdict` filters on that effective verdict. No approval needed — it only reads.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

since.description: Only requests at or after this ISO date-time.

tools.name: brain_feedback_record
tools.title: Record human feedback on a request, note, memory, fact or proposal
tools.description: Append-only write of one human verdict (certo, parcial, errado, nao-sei) with an optional reason and note. Human role only: the caller must be the owner (POST /mcp with the owner token as bearer); every agent caller, stdio included, is refused and nothing is written. The actor is the authenticated principal. Recording again on the same target supersedes the previous event (it is never edited). The note is untrusted text: capped, PII/instruction flagged, never sent to Jev. Reversible by supersession; LGPD erasure clears the note.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_feedback_list
tools.title: Feedback events of the brain
tools.description: Read-only list of feedback events, newest first: by default only the current event per actor and target; include_superseded shows the history. Filter by target, surface, actor or time. Notes are returned to the human owner only; an agent caller gets each event without its note. No approval needed — it only reads.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_list
tools.title: Lacunas de conhecimento — questions the brain could not answer
tools.description: Read-only list of knowledge gaps, most recently updated first: questions the brain found it could not answer, clustered by near-duplicate text so repeats become one row with a count. Found automatically from three sources — real requests with a gap outcome, bench misses whose miss stage is not-retrieved, and Curadoria verdicts recorded falta-conhecimento — and merged fresh before every answer, so no separate scan is needed. No approval needed — it only reads.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_decide
tools.title: Record a human direction on a knowledge gap
tools.description: Records the direction a human picked for one open gap: corrigir (fix a note), adicionar (add new content), remover (archive an outdated note), or nao_aplica (the question does not apply). Human role only: the caller must be the owner (POST /mcp with the owner token as bearer); every agent caller, stdio included, is refused and nothing is written. note and target_note are untrusted free text: capped and scanned for PII/injection the same way a feedback note is, and the resulting flags are stored on the gap. Slice 1 stops at recording the direction — drafting the fix as a proposal is a later slice.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_draft
tools.title: Draft a fix for a directed knowledge gap
tools.description: The brain drafts the fix a human already directed (corrigir/adicionar/remover), grounded in the nearest sources plus the human's note, and stages it as an inert vault-note proposal — nothing touches the vault yet. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions direcionada -> proposta_pendente.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_approve
tools.title: Approve a gap's drafted fix — write, sync, re-ask
tools.description: Approves the gap's pending draft (signs the decision with the brain's local owner authority — this call IS the human's explicit approval), applies it to the vault, runs the same sync pass `brain sync` runs, then re-asks the gap's question(s) and marks it Resolvida (a cited answer now covers it) or Reaberta. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions proposta_pendente -> aplicada_reconferindo -> resolvida|reaberta.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_discard
tools.title: Discard a gap's drafted fix
tools.description: Withdraws the gap's pending draft without applying it (a signature-free dismissal — nothing was ever written to the vault) and reopens the gap. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions proposta_pendente -> aberta.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_adjust
tools.title: Redirect a gap's drafted fix and draft again
tools.description: Discards the gap's pending draft, records a fresh direction from the human's new note (same direction kind, updated note/target note), and immediately drafts again. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions proposta_pendente -> aberta -> direcionada -> proposta_pendente.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_events

tools.description: Read-only, oldest first: the append-only event trail behind one knowledge gap (direção, rascunho, aprovado, ajustado, descartado, reconferido), including a rejected draft a later one has since overwritten on the gap's own row. No approval needed — it only reads. An agent-role caller never gets an event's note text (it may carry PII); only the human owner does.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_activity_since
tools.title: Activity since — committed requests after a sequence
tools.description: Read-only. Returns the brain's committed requests (search, ask, recall, sync …) observed after `since_seq`, as Studio activity phrases, plus the new `since_seq` to continue from. A missing, other-epoch or too-old `since_seq` gets a snapshot (`snapshot: true`, the latest phrases) instead of a gap. Non-streaming twin of brain_activity_watch.

since_seq.description: The since_seq a previous brain_activity_watch/brain_activity_since returned; omit for a snapshot.

brain_id.description: Brain to watch; defaults to the request's brain.

tools.name: brain_activity_watch
tools.title: Activity watch — stream committed requests live
tools.description: Read-only, request-scoped stream. Polls the brain's committed requests for up to `max_seconds` (default 25, max 55) and sends each new one as a progress notification when the call carries `_meta.progressToken` (`message` = the phrase as JSON, `progress` = its seq). Ends with `since_seq` and the phrases it saw; call again with that `since_seq` to keep watching. A missing, other-epoch or too-old `since_seq` returns a snapshot at once.

since_seq.description: The since_seq a previous brain_activity_watch/brain_activity_since returned; omit for a snapshot.

max_seconds.description: How long to watch, in seconds (default 25).

brain_id.description: Brain to watch; defaults to the request's brain.

tools.name: brain_growth_snapshot
tools.title: Growth snapshot — the brain as subjects over time
tools.description: Read-only snapshot for Studio's growth view: the brain's notes grouped into subjects (algorithm subjects-v1, seed pastas+tags: folders refined by owner tags; memory episodes on their own lane), the links between subjects, facts/memories/proposals as dated events, and query traces with the notes they touched. Every timestamp names its source (indexado-em, created_at). Query and memory text appear only when the brain opted in to query text; otherwise hashes and neutral labels. Scope: the optional `brain_id` (otherwise the server's brain). No approval needed — it only reads the brain; it keeps the last subject ids under $BRAIN_HOME/state so a subject keeps its id across re-index.

brain_id.description: Brain to snapshot; defaults to the server's brain.

tools.name: brain_settings_get
tools.title: Settings — this brain's settings and the install's, with sources
tools.description: Read-only view of Studio's Configurações. `rows`: one per control of the settings registry, with its store, the stored value, the value the answering process runs with and where that came from, whether a change needs a restart, what leaves the machine when it is on, and the action the page may take (set, restart or none, with a reason when it cannot). tools.name: brain_plugin_install_preview
tools.title: Plugins — preview installing the E-mail plugin's wk
tools.description: Read-only. What turning the E-mail plugin on would download: the pinned workit (wk) version, its release archive URL, both digests (the archive's own sha256 and the extracted wk binary's sha256 — `sha256` echoes the binary digest, the one to confirm), where the verified copy would be written, this machine's platform, and whether that platform is supported. Also names, in `signInScopes`, the exact Google OAuth scopes a LATER brain_plugin_signin will request (Gmail read-only plus the OIDC identity scopes every sign-in gets — openid, email, userinfo.email), and in `signInEgress`, that the login passes through workit's own hosted relay, auth.automagik.dev (a first-party Namastex service), which returns the authorization to this machine. tools.name: brain_plugin_install
tools.title: Plugins — install the E-mail plugin's wk (owner only, verified)
tools.description: Downloads the pinned workit (wk) release archive over HTTPS, verifies the ARCHIVE's sha256, decompresses and parses it in process, extracts only the wk member, then verifies the extracted BINARY's own sha256 — before writing a single executable byte — installs the verified copy and writes wk.json. Refuses unless `sha256` equals exactly the binary digest brain_plugin_install_preview returned (echo the preview; never guess it). Human role only: every agent caller, stdio included, is refused and nothing is written. A digest mismatch, at any of the three checks, writes nothing.

tools.title: Context recall — session episodic + identity memory
tools.description: Read-only recall of the current session's episodic memory plus durable identity/user context — never writes. Scope: the optional `brain_id` (otherwise BRAIN_ID or the nearest `.brain/config.json` from the caller-provided project working directory (or the MCP process working directory when absent)), limited to the request metadata session id (falling back to BRAIN_KHORTEX_SESSION, read at call time and REQUIRED; when both are unset this tool refuses with a scoped-session-required error and runs no query, since an unscoped cross-session recall is an unauthenticated data exposure). Precedence: when the call carries a session id, that session's PINNED brain outranks `brain_id` — the answer then comes from the pinned brain, the output names both brains in a `brain override:` line, and the serve logs the ignored drift. No approval needed — it only reads. Trust: completeness promise — if it happened it is found; if it did not, this tool says so plainly rather than guessing, and grounded answers carry provenance. Reversible by nature: a read changes nothing.

tools.name: brain_requests_list

Each row names the notes the request returned (top 10 hits), its outcome, confidence and latency. Query text appears only when the brain opted in (brains.query_text_opt_in, default off); otherwise the row carries its sha256 alone. Verdicts come from brain_feedback_events: a human verdict outranks a machine one, and `verdict` filters on that effective verdict. No approval needed — it only reads.

tools.name: brain_feedback_record
tools.title: Record human feedback on a request, note, memory, fact or proposal
tools.description: Append-only write of one human verdict (certo, parcial, errado, nao-sei) with an optional reason and note. Human role only: the caller must be the owner (POST /mcp with the owner token as bearer); every agent caller, stdio included, is refused and nothing is written. The actor is the authenticated principal. Recording again on the same target supersedes the previous event (it is never edited). The note is untrusted text: capped, PII/instruction flagged, never sent to Jev. Reversible by supersession; LGPD erasure clears the note.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_feedback_list
tools.title: Feedback events of the brain
tools.description: Read-only list of feedback events, newest first: by default only the current event per actor and target; include_superseded shows the history. Filter by target, surface, actor or time. Notes are returned to the human owner only; an agent caller gets each event without its note. No approval needed — it only reads.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_list
tools.title: Lacunas de conhecimento — questions the brain could not answer
tools.description: Read-only list of knowledge gaps, most recently updated first: questions the brain found it could not answer, clustered by near-duplicate text so repeats become one row with a count. Found automatically from three sources — real requests with a gap outcome, bench misses whose miss stage is not-retrieved, and Curadoria verdicts recorded falta-conhecimento — and merged fresh before every answer, so no separate scan is needed. No approval needed — it only reads.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_decide
tools.title: Record a human direction on a knowledge gap
tools.description: Records the direction a human picked for one open gap: corrigir (fix a note), adicionar (add new content), remover (archive an outdated note), or nao_aplica (the question does not apply). Human role only: the caller must be the owner (POST /mcp with the owner token as bearer); every agent caller, stdio included, is refused and nothing is written. note and target_note are untrusted free text: capped and scanned for PII/injection the same way a feedback note is, and the resulting flags are stored on the gap. Slice 1 stops at recording the direction — drafting the fix as a proposal is a later slice.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_draft
tools.title: Draft a fix for a directed knowledge gap
tools.description: The brain drafts the fix a human already directed (corrigir/adicionar/remover), grounded in the nearest sources plus the human's note, and stages it as an inert vault-note proposal — nothing touches the vault yet. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions direcionada -> proposta_pendente.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_approve
tools.title: Approve a gap's drafted fix — write, sync, re-ask
tools.description: Approves the gap's pending draft (signs the decision with the brain's local owner authority — this call IS the human's explicit approval), applies it to the vault, runs the same sync pass `brain sync` runs, then re-asks the gap's question(s) and marks it Resolvida (a cited answer now covers it) or Reaberta. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions proposta_pendente -> aplicada_reconferindo -> resolvida|reaberta.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_discard
tools.title: Discard a gap's drafted fix
tools.description: Withdraws the gap's pending draft without applying it (a signature-free dismissal — nothing was ever written to the vault) and reopens the gap. Human role only, same gate as brain_gap_decide. Transitions proposta_pendente -> aberta.

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

tools.name: brain_gap_adjust
tools.title: Redirect a gap's drafted fix and draft again

brain_id.description: Brain to read or write; defaults to the request's brain (the serve's rooted brain, `?brain_id=`, BRAIN_ID or the nearest .brain/config.json).

Ends with `since_seq` and the phrases it saw; call again with that `since_seq` to keep watching. A missing, other-epoch or too-old `since_seq` returns a snapshot at once.

since_seq.description: The since_seq a previous brain_activity_watch/brain_activity_since returned; omit for a snapshot.

tools.name: brain_plugin_install_preview
tools.title: Plugins — preview installing the E-mail plugin's wk
tools.description: Read-only. What turning the E-mail plugin on would download: the pinned workit (wk) version, its release archive URL, both digests (the archive's own sha256 and the extracted wk binary's sha256 — `sha256` echoes the binary digest, the one to confirm), where the verified copy would be written, this machine's platform, and whether that platform is supported. Also names, in `signInScopes`, the exact Google OAuth scopes a LATER brain_plugin_signin will request (Gmail read-only plus the OIDC identity scopes every sign-in gets — openid, email, userinfo.email), and in `signInEgress`, that the login passes through workit's own hosted relay, auth.automagik.dev (a first-party Namastex service), which returns the authorization to this machine. Nothing is downloaded, decompressed or written. Any principal.

plugin.description: The plugin to act on. Only "email" is implemented.

tools.name: brain_plugin_install
tools.title: Plugins — install the E-mail plugin's wk (owner only, verified)
tools.description: Downloads the pinned workit (wk) release archive over HTTPS, verifies the ARCHIVE's sha256, decompresses and parses it in process, extracts only the wk member, then verifies the extracted BINARY's own sha256 — before writing a single executable byte — installs the verified copy and writes wk.json. Refuses unless `sha256` equals exactly the binary digest brain_plugin_install_preview returned (echo the preview; never guess it). Human role only: every agent caller, stdio included, is refused and nothing is written. A digest mismatch, at any of the three checks, writes nothing.

plugin.description: The plugin to act on. Only "email" is implemented.

sha256.description: The binary sha256 brain_plugin_install_preview returned; echoed back to confirm.

tools.name: brain_plugin_signin
tools.title: Plugins — start Google's read-only sign-in (owner only)
tools.description: Starts wk's read-only Google sign-in for `email` (spawns the verified wk with `auth add <email> --headless --readonly --services gmail --client brain-ro`). `email` must be the exact Google account address you will authorize in the browser — wk itself refuses to store the token otherwise; `label` is only brain's own wk.json key for this account (e.g. "work") and is never sent to wk. Returns an authUrl to open in a browser, a sessionId to poll with brain_plugin_signin_status, the exact `scopes` this sign-in requests (Gmail read-only plus openid/email/userinfo.email — nothing else), and an `egress` line: the login passes through workit's own hosted relay, auth.automagik.dev (a first-party Namastex service), which returns the authorization to this machine. Human role only: every agent caller, stdio included, is refused.

plugin.description: The plugin to act on. Only "email" is implemented.

label.description: The wk.json account label to create, e.g. "work".

email.description: The exact Google account address you will sign in as — wk's own `auth add <email>` argument. wk refuses to store the token unless the account actually authorized in the browser matches this exactly.

tools.name: brain_plugin_signin_status
tools.title: Plugins — poll a sign-in session
tools.description: Read-only. The state of a sign-in session started by brain_plugin_signin: waiting, done, expired, or refused (with a fix — e.g. a full-scope token is refused with "Entrar de novo (só leitura)"). `expired` covers a denied consent, an abandoned tab AND a relay outage during the poll — wk's own `--headless` flow cannot tell them apart, so this never claims more certainty than wk has. On done, the account is already recorded in wk.json. Any principal.

tools.name: brain_plugin_uninstall
tools.title: Plugins — uninstall the E-mail plugin's wk (owner only)
tools.description: Removes the verified wk copy and wk.json. The Google account's token stays in workit's own keyring — this does not sign it out or revoke it.
